Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1960
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T14:50:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.
- `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` + batched `test/cli` runs: native `malloc_consolidate` abort at runner teardown (sandbox PTY issue); all tests pass — run that file standalone.
- `test/browser_ext` e2e: setUpAll needs a browser fixture not present in this sandbox.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user

- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent

  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

+/// coalesce, retry once) and the issue #85 pairing heal's detection
+/// helper plus the [ToolPairingRepairEvent] it emits. Split out of
+/// `agent_loop.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate.
+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the
+/// loop's private members.
+part of 'agent_loop.dart';
+
+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
+/// once per response when the provider refused the request because the
+/// message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap (`array length N exceeds
+/// limit M`). The host runs ONE synchronous compaction pass over the live
+/// transcript (the summary is the real message-count reducer; the loop's
+/// own coalesce only merges whole tool pairs on the outbound payload) and
+/// returns the relieved transcript to retry with — or `null` when nothing
+/// hideable remains (the retry then rides the coalesced payload alone;
+/// a second refusal surfaces the terminal error). The argument is the
+/// loop's live transcript; the returned list REPLACES it for the rest of
+/// the run. `null` = no relief configured: the retry still runs once with
+/// the coalesced payload (then the refusal is terminal).
+typedef MessageCapRelief =
+    Future<List<Message>?> Function(List<Message> overCapMessages);
+
+/// Emitted when the outbound request context needed tool-pairing surgery
+/// (issue #85): orphaned tool results dropped, missing results synthesized,
+/// or duplicate ids renamed. Repairs are never silent — [report] carries
+/// the counts and affected ids, and [providerError] is set when the pass
+/// ran in response to a provider pairing error (the self-healing retry).
+final class ToolPairingRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const ToolPairingRepairEvent({required this.report, this.providerError});
+
+  /// What the repair changed (empty report = detection only).
+  final ToolPairingRepairReport report;
+
+  /// Raw provider error that triggered this pass, when it ran on the
+  /// retry path; null for the pre-request repair.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Emitted when the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal ran: the provider refused
+/// the request because the message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap
+/// (`array length N exceeds limit M`). The cap was learned per model, the
+/// outbound payload was coalesced (outbound-only — the session JSONL is

+/// compaction pass ran before the single retry. Repairs are never silent.
+final class MessageCapRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const MessageCapRepairEvent({
+    required this.messageCount,
+    this.learnedCap,
+    this.compacted = false,
+    this.providerError,
+  });
+
+  /// The message count that rode the refused request — the number the
+  /// provider's cap refused.
+  final int messageCount;
+
+  /// The cap learned from the refusal text; null when the refusal carried
+  /// no parseable limit (cap-unknown, edge E1).
+  final int? learnedCap;
+
+  /// Whether a host compaction pass ran over the live transcript before
+  /// the retry (the [MessageCapRelief] answered non-null).
+  final bool compacted;
+
+  /// The raw provider error that triggered the heal.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot pairing self-heal (issue
+/// #85): a provider pairing 400 on an error stop, before it was used.
+bool _needsPairingHeal(bool pairingHealed, AssistantMessage finished) =>
+    !pairingHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    isToolPairingProviderError(finished.errorMessage);
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot message-cap self-heal
+/// (gh-1680): a classified cap refusal on an error stop, with a policy
+/// configured, before it was used.
+bool _needsCapHeal(
+  bool capHealed,
+  AssistantMessage finished,
+  AgentLoopConfig config,
+) =>
+    !capHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    config.messageCapPolicy != null &&
+    classifyMessageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null;
+
+/// The mutable gh-1680 heal state of one streamed response: whether the
+/// one-shot heal already ran, and the coalesce target the next rebuilt
+/// payload rides toward (armed by the heal, null when the cap is
+/// unknown). Mirrors how `reliefUsed`/`pairingHealed` stay loop-local.
+final class _CapHealState {
+  bool healed = false;
+
+  /// The coalesce target for `_buildRequestContext` (learned cap −

+  int? coalesceTarget;
+
+  /// Runs the one-shot heal when [finished] is a classified cap refusal.

+  healIfNeeded(

+    Context context,
+    AgentLoopConfig config,
+    AgentEventSink emit,
+    CancelToken? cancelToken,
+    int refusedCount,

## PR Description

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

index 0000000000..076db31ed6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/src/agent/agent_loop_message_cap.dart
@@ -0,0 +1,219 @@
+/// The one-shot self-heal repairs of the response stream: the gh-1680
+/// message-cap heal (learn the cap from the provider's refusal, compact +
+/// coalesce, retry once) and the issue #85 pairing heal's detection
+/// helper plus the [ToolPairingRepairEvent] it emits. Split out of
+/// `agent_loop.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate.
+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the
+/// loop's private members.
+part of 'agent_loop.dart';
+
+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
+/// once per response when the provider refused the request because the
+/// message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap (`array length N exceeds
+/// limit M`). The host runs ONE synchronous compaction pass over the live
+/// transcript (the summary is the real message-count reducer; the loop's
+/// own coalesce only merges whole tool pairs on the outbound payload) and
+/// returns the relieved transcript to retry with — or `null` when nothing
+/// hideable remains (the retry then rides the coalesced payload alone;
+/// a second refusal surfaces the terminal error). The argument is the
+/// loop's live transcript; the returned list REPLACES it for the rest of
+/// the run. `null` = no relief configured: the retry still runs once with
+/// the coalesced payload (then the refusal is terminal).
+typedef MessageCapRelief =
+    Future<List<Message>?> Function(List<Message> overCapMessages);
+
+/// Emitted when the outbound request context needed tool-pairing surgery
+/// (issue #85): orphaned tool results dropped, missing results synthesized,
+/// or duplicate ids renamed. Repairs are never silent — [report] carries
+/// the counts and affected ids, and [providerError] is set when the pass
+/// ran in response to a provider pairing error (the self-healing retry).
+final class ToolPairingRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const ToolPairingRepairEvent({required this.report, this.providerError});
+
+  /// What the repair changed (empty report = detection only).
+  final ToolPairingRepairReport report;
+
+  /// Raw provider error that triggered this pass, when it ran on the
+  /// retry path; null for the pre-request repair.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Emitted when the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal ran: the provider refused
+/// the request because the message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap
+/// (`array length N exceeds limit M`). The cap was learned per model, the
+/// outbound payload was coalesced (outbound-only — the session JSONL is
+/// byte-identical), and — when the host configured [MessageCapRelief] — a
+/// compaction pass ran before the single retry. Repairs are never silent.
+final class MessageCapRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const MessageCapRepairEvent({
+    required this.messageCount,
+    this.learnedCap,
+    this.compacted = false,
+    this.providerError,
+  });
+
+  /// The message count that rode the refused request — the number the
+  /// provider's cap refused.
+  final int messageCount;
+
+  /// The cap learned from the refusal text; null when the refusal carried
+  /// no parseable limit (cap-unknown, edge E1).
+  final int? learnedCap;
+
+  /// Whether a host compaction pass ran over the live transcript before
+  /// the retry (the [MessageCapRelief] answered non-null).
+  final bool compacted;
+
+  /// The raw provider error that triggered the heal.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot pairing self-heal (issue
+/// #85): a provider pairing 400 on an error stop, before it was used.
+bool _needsPairingHeal(bool pairingHealed, AssistantMessage finished) =>
+    !pairingHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    isToolPairingProviderError(finished.errorMessage);
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot message-cap self-heal
+/// (gh-1680): a classified cap refusal on an error stop, with a policy
+/// configured, before it was used.
+bool _needsCapHeal(
+  bool capHealed,
+  AssistantMessage finished,
+  AgentLoopConfig config,
+) =>
+    !capHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    config.messageCapPolicy != null &&
+    classifyMessageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null;
+

- **Author**: ai-teammate

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.

+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the

+part of 'agent_loop.dart';

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1960
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T14:50:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.

- `test/browser_ext` e2e: setUpAll needs a browser fixture not present in this sandbox.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.

+/// message-cap heal (learn the cap from the provider's refusal, compact +
+/// coalesce, retry once) and the issue #85 pairing heal's detection
+/// helper plus the [ToolPairingRepairEvent] it emits. Split out of
+/// `agent_loop.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate.
+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the
+/// loop's private members.
+part of 'agent_loop.dart';
+
+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
+/// once per response when the provider refused the request because the
+/// message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap (`array length N exceeds
+/// limit M`). The host runs ONE synchronous compaction pass over the live
+/// transcript (the summary is the real message-count reducer; the loop's
+/// own coalesce only merges whole tool pairs on the outbound payload) and
+/// returns the relieved transcript to retry with — or `null` when nothing
+/// hideable remains (the retry then rides the coalesced payload alone;
+/// a second refusal surfaces the terminal error). The argument is the
+/// loop's live transcript; the returned list REPLACES it for the rest of
+/// the run. `null` = no relief configured: the retry still runs once with
+/// the coalesced payload (then the refusal is terminal).
+typedef MessageCapRelief =
+    Future<List<Message>?> Function(List<Message> overCapMessages);
+
+/// Emitted when the outbound request context needed tool-pairing surgery
+/// (issue #85): orphaned tool results dropped, missing results synthesized,
+/// or duplicate ids renamed. Repairs are never silent — [report] carries
+/// the counts and affected ids, and [providerError] is set when the pass
+/// ran in response to a provider pairing error (the self-healing retry).
+final class ToolPairingRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const ToolPairingRepairEvent({required this.report, this.providerError});
+
+  /// What the repair changed (empty report = detection only).
+  final ToolPairingRepairReport report;
+
+  /// Raw provider error that triggered this pass, when it ran on the
+  /// retry path; null for the pre-request repair.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Emitted when the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal ran: the provider refused
+/// the request because the message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap
+/// (`array length N exceeds limit M`). The cap was learned per model, the
+/// outbound payload was coalesced (outbound-only — the session JSONL is
+/// byte-identical), and — when the host configured [MessageCapRelief] — a
+/// compaction pass ran before the single retry. Repairs are never silent.
+final class MessageCapRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const MessageCapRepairEvent({
+    required this.messageCount,
+    this.learnedCap,
+    this.compacted = false,
+    this.providerError,
+  });
+
+  /// The message count that rode the refused request — the number the
+  /// provider's cap refused.
+  final int messageCount;
+
+  /// The cap learned from the refusal text; null when the refusal carried
+  /// no parseable limit (cap-unknown, edge E1).
+  final int? learnedCap;
+
+  /// Whether a host compaction pass ran over the live transcript before
+  /// the retry (the [MessageCapRelief] answered non-null).
+  final bool compacted;
+
+  /// The raw provider error that triggered the heal.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot pairing self-heal (issue
+/// #85): a provider pairing 400 on an error stop, before it was used.
+bool _needsPairingHeal(bool pairingHealed, AssistantMessage finished) =>
+    !pairingHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    isToolPairingProviderError(finished.errorMessage);
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot message-cap self-heal
+/// (gh-1680): a classified cap refusal on an error stop, with a policy
+/// configured, before it was used.
+bool _needsCapHeal(
+  bool capHealed,
+  AssistantMessage finished,
+  AgentLoopConfig config,
+) =>
+    !capHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    config.messageCapPolicy != null &&
+    classifyMessageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null;
+
+/// The mutable gh-1680 heal state of one streamed response: whether the
+/// one-shot heal already ran, and the coalesce target the next rebuilt
+/// payload rides toward (armed by the heal, null when the cap is

+  bool healed = false;
+
+  /// The coalesce target for `_buildRequestContext` (learned cap −

+  int? coalesceTarget;
+
+  /// Runs the one-shot heal when [finished] is a classified cap refusal.

+  Future<({bool ran, Context? context, (AssistantMessage, Context)? terminal})>
+  healIfNeeded(
+    AssistantMessage finished,
+    Context context,
+    AgentLoopConfig config,
+    AgentEventSink emit,
+    CancelToken? cancelToken,
+    int refusedCount,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1960
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T14:50:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+    this.learnedCap,

+    this.providerError,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1960
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T14:50:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.
- `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` + batched `test/cli` runs: native `malloc_consolidate` abort at runner teardown (sandbox PTY issue); all tests pass — run that file standalone.
- `test/browser_ext` e2e: setUpAll needs a browser fixture not present in this sandbox.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

+/// The one-shot self-heal repairs of the response stream: the gh-1680
+/// message-cap heal (learn the cap from the provider's refusal, compact +
+/// coalesce, retry once) and the issue #85 pairing heal's detection
+/// helper plus the [ToolPairingRepairEvent] it emits. Split out of
+/// `agent_loop.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate.
+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the
+/// loop's private members.
+part of 'agent_loop.dart';
+
+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
+/// once per response when the provider refused the request because the
+/// message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap (`array length N exceeds
+/// limit M`). The host runs ONE synchronous compaction pass over the live
+/// transcript (the summary is the real message-count reducer; the loop's
+/// own coalesce only merges whole tool pairs on the outbound payload) and
+/// returns the relieved transcript to retry with — or `null` when nothing
+/// hideable remains (the retry then rides the coalesced payload alone;
+/// a second refusal surfaces the terminal error). The argument is the
+/// loop's live transcript; the returned list REPLACES it for the rest of
+/// the run. `null` = no relief configured: the retry still runs once with
+/// the coalesced payload (then the refusal is terminal).
+typedef MessageCapRelief =
+    Future<List<Message>?> Function(List<Message> overCapMessages);
+
+/// Emitted when the outbound request context needed tool-pairing surgery
+/// (issue #85): orphaned tool results dropped, missing results synthesized,
+/// or duplicate ids renamed. Repairs are never silent — [report] carries
+/// the counts and affected ids, and [providerError] is set when the pass
+/// ran in response to a provider pairing error (the self-healing retry).
+final class ToolPairingRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const ToolPairingRepairEvent({required this.report, this.providerError});
+
+  /// What the repair changed (empty report = detection only).
+  final ToolPairingRepairReport report;
+
+  /// Raw provider error that triggered this pass, when it ran on the
+  /// retry path; null for the pre-request repair.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Emitted when the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal ran: the provider refused

+/// compaction pass ran before the single retry. Repairs are never silent.
+final class MessageCapRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const MessageCapRepairEvent({
+    required this.messageCount,
+    this.learnedCap,
+    this.compacted = false,
+    this.providerError,
+  });
+
+  /// The message count that rode the refused request — the number the
+  /// provider's cap refused.
+  final int messageCount;
+
+  /// The cap learned from the refusal text; null when the refusal carried
+  /// no parseable limit (cap-unknown, edge E1).
+  final int? learnedCap;
+
+  /// Whether a host compaction pass ran over the live transcript before
+  /// the retry (the [MessageCapRelief] answered non-null).
+  final bool compacted;
+
+  /// The raw provider error that triggered the heal.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot pairing self-heal (issue
+/// #85): a provider pairing 400 on an error stop, before it was used.
+bool _needsPairingHeal(bool pairingHealed, AssistantMessage finished) =>
+    !pairingHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&

+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot message-cap self-heal
+/// (gh-1680): a classified cap refusal on an error stop, with a policy
+/// configured, before it was used.
+bool _needsCapHeal(
+  bool capHealed,
+  AssistantMessage finished,
+  AgentLoopConfig config,
+) =>
+    !capHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    config.messageCapPolicy != null &&
+    classifyMessageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null;
+
+/// The mutable gh-1680 heal state of one streamed response: whether the
+/// one-shot heal already ran, and the coalesce target the next rebuilt
+/// payload rides toward (armed by the heal, null when the cap is
+/// unknown). Mirrors how `reliefUsed`/`pairingHealed` stay loop-local.
+final class _CapHealState {
+  bool healed = false;
+
+  /// The coalesce target for `_buildRequestContext` (learned cap −

+  int? coalesceTarget;
+
+  /// Runs the one-shot heal when [finished] is a classified cap refusal.
+  /// [refusedCount] is the refused payload's message count, captured by

+  /// context for the retry.
+  Future<({bool ran, Context? context, (AssistantMessage, Context)? terminal})>
+  healIfNeeded(
+    AssistantMessage finished,
+    Context context,
+    AgentLoopConfig config,
+    AgentEventSink emit,
+    CancelToken? cancelToken,
+    int refusedCount,

+  int? coalesceTarget,
+  (AssistantMessage, Context)? terminal,

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1695
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1695
- **Title**: gh-1680 [GOAL] Adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, pre-emptive compaction before the cap (dmtools-factory 01a14b3a wedge no hardcoded provider tables)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1680` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1960
- **Deletions**: -45
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T14:37:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T14:50:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

+++ b/lib/src/agent/agent_loop_message_cap.dart
@@ -0,0 +1,219 @@
+/// The one-shot self-heal repairs of the response stream: the gh-1680
+/// message-cap heal (learn the cap from the provider's refusal, compact +
+/// coalesce, retry once) and the issue #85 pairing heal's detection
+/// helper plus the [ToolPairingRepairEvent] it emits. Split out of
+/// `agent_loop.dart` to keep it under the repo's 2800-line size gate.
+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the
+/// loop's private members.
+part of 'agent_loop.dart';
+
+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
+/// once per response when the provider refused the request because the
+/// message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap (`array length N exceeds
+/// limit M`). The host runs ONE synchronous compaction pass over the live
+/// transcript (the summary is the real message-count reducer; the loop's
+/// own coalesce only merges whole tool pairs on the outbound payload) and
+/// returns the relieved transcript to retry with — or `null` when nothing
+/// hideable remains (the retry then rides the coalesced payload alone;
+/// a second refusal surfaces the terminal error). The argument is the
+/// loop's live transcript; the returned list REPLACES it for the rest of
+/// the run. `null` = no relief configured: the retry still runs once with
+/// the coalesced payload (then the refusal is terminal).
+typedef MessageCapRelief =
+    Future<List<Message>?> Function(List<Message> overCapMessages);
+
+/// Emitted when the outbound request context needed tool-pairing surgery
+/// (issue #85): orphaned tool results dropped, missing results synthesized,
+/// or duplicate ids renamed. Repairs are never silent — [report] carries
+/// the counts and affected ids, and [providerError] is set when the pass
+/// ran in response to a provider pairing error (the self-healing retry).
+final class ToolPairingRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const ToolPairingRepairEvent({required this.report, this.providerError});
+
+  /// What the repair changed (empty report = detection only).
+  final ToolPairingRepairReport report;
+
+  /// Raw provider error that triggered this pass, when it ran on the
+  /// retry path; null for the pre-request repair.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Emitted when the gh-1680 message-cap self-heal ran: the provider refused
+/// the request because the message ARRAY exceeded its per-request cap
+/// (`array length N exceeds limit M`). The cap was learned per model, the
+/// outbound payload was coalesced (outbound-only — the session JSONL is
+/// byte-identical), and — when the host configured [MessageCapRelief] — a
+/// compaction pass ran before the single retry. Repairs are never silent.
+final class MessageCapRepairEvent extends AgentEvent {
+  const MessageCapRepairEvent({
+    required this.messageCount,
+    this.learnedCap,
+    this.compacted = false,
+    this.providerError,
+  });
+
+  /// The message count that rode the refused request — the number the
+  /// provider's cap refused.
+  final int messageCount;
+
+  /// The cap learned from the refusal text; null when the refusal carried
+  /// no parseable limit (cap-unknown, edge E1).
+  final int? learnedCap;
+
+  /// Whether a host compaction pass ran over the live transcript before
+  /// the retry (the [MessageCapRelief] answered non-null).
+  final bool compacted;
+
+  /// The raw provider error that triggered the heal.
+  final String? providerError;
+}
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot pairing self-heal (issue
+/// #85): a provider pairing 400 on an error stop, before it was used.
+bool _needsPairingHeal(bool pairingHealed, AssistantMessage finished) =>
+    !pairingHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    isToolPairingProviderError(finished.errorMessage);
+
+/// Whether a finished turn needs the one-shot message-cap self-heal
+/// (gh-1680): a classified cap refusal on an error stop, with a policy
+/// configured, before it was used.
+bool _needsCapHeal(
+  bool capHealed,
+  AssistantMessage finished,
+  AgentLoopConfig config,
+) =>
+    !capHealed &&
+    finished.stopReason == StopReason.error &&
+    config.messageCapPolicy != null &&
+    classifyMessageCapError(finished.errorMessage) != null;
+
+/// The mutable gh-1680 heal state of one streamed response: whether the
+/// one-shot heal already ran, and the coalesce target the next rebuilt
+/// payload rides toward (armed by the heal, null when the cap is
+/// unknown). Mirrors how `reliefUsed`/`pairingHealed` stay loop-local.
+final class _CapHealState {
+  bool healed = false;
+
+  /// The coalesce target for `_buildRequestContext` (learned cap −
+  /// margin); null = nothing armed / cap unknown.
+  int? coalesceTarget;
+
+  /// Runs the one-shot heal when [finished] is a classified cap refusal.
+  /// [refusedCount] is the refused payload's message count, captured by
+  /// the caller BEFORE the stream (the streamed partial mutates the live

- **Author**: ai-teammate

## PR Description

Closes #1680
### What changed
gh-1680 adaptive per-model message-cap handling: a provider refusal like `400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048` is now classified (`classifyMessageCapError`), the cap is learned per model in `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json` (`MessageCapPolicy`), and the loop heals once — host compaction pass + payload-only coalesce — then retries exactly once. Once any cap is known, compaction also fires pre-emptively on message count (next-request projection), never letting the session wedge in the first place.

### Key decisions
- **One-shot heal** in the response stream (`agent_loop_message_cap.dart` part): learn → `MessageCapRelief` (host compaction) → arm coalesce → retry once; second refusal is terminal, transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical).
- **Coalesce is outbound-only**: `coalesceMessagesForCap` merges whole tool-call/result pairs and old turns older than the newest user message into compact carriers; never drops the running turn or mid-pair blocks.
- **Cap-unknown edge (E1)**: no parseable limit → no coalesce target, relief-only retry.
- **Pre-emptive gate in `AutoCompactor`** rides the existing `CompactionTrigger` slot alongside the token window, so headless gets it for free; CLI wires the policy, relief (structured engine), `/context` caps line, ledger row, and TUI event (emits `compact_phase` + compaction notice, mirrors the over-window relief).
- **Wire**: new `message_cap_repair` event (kind + counts, no text); stream-json filters it as fa-internal; tripwire test extended.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/message_cap_loop_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_store_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_coalesce_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_compactor_test.dart test/agent/message_cap_source_scan_test.dart test/overflow_test.dart
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request refused: 400 array length N exceeds limit M] --> CLS[classifyMessageCapError]
  CLS --> LEARN[MessageCapPolicy.learnFromRefusal → ~/.fah/model-message-caps.json]
  LEARN --> RELIEF[MessageCapRelief: ONE structured compaction]
  LEARN --> COAL[arm coalesce target = cap − margin]
  RELIEF --> RETRY[Retry once]
  COAL --> RETRY
  RETRY -->|refused again| ERR[Terminal error — no loop]
  KNOWN[Cap known] --> GATE[AutoCompactor pre-emptive gate: projected msgs ≥ cap → compact]
```

</details>

### Known pre-existing failures (verified identical on base 096b36d, not regressions)
- `test/integration/headless_log_file_test.dart` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test.dart` (2), `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` (1): the sandbox leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` into test children — same failures on base.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,

+/// Same library (a `part of`), so the helpers keep their access to the

+part of 'agent_loop.dart';

+/// gh-1680: emergency relief for the message-cap self-heal. Called at most
