blocks.text:
rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Variants (`messages: array length 2051 exceeds limit 2048`, `array length N exceeds limit M`, `too many messages`, `messages count exceeds`) classify; non-overflow 400s (auth, bad request) do not. (`UT-1`)
- **AC2** — After one cap-400, `(provider, modelId)` is marked with the learned cap; the record persists across restarts and is boot-loaded. (`UT-2`, `IT-1`)
- **AC3** — Reactive: a classified cap-400 coalesces + runs one compaction pass + retries once; the retry succeeds; a second cap-400 surfaces the terminal; no infinite loop. (`IT-2`, `E2E-1`)
- **AC4** — Pre-emptive: a model with a learned cap triggers compaction when the live count reaches `cap − margin`, BEFORE the request; the request rides the compacted array (no doomed round-trip). (`IT-3`, `E2E-2`)
- **AC5** — No provider/model name is hardcoded anywhere in the repair path (source-scan asserts the classifier is the only built-in). (`UT-3`, `REG-1`)
- **AC6** — Coalesce preserves tool-call/result pairing (the `tool_pairing` repairer's invariants hold on the wire) and never drops the newest user message or the system prompt. (`UT-4`)
- **AC7** — The session JSONL is byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only). (`UT-5`, `REG-2`)
- **AC8** — A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today; token compaction semantics unchanged. (`REG-3`)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-1` — classifier: incident string + variants → overflow + parsed `M`; auth/other 400s unchanged; unparseable cap (`array length exceeds limit` without a number) → flagged cap-unknown.
- `UT-2` — learned-cap store: parse→record→persist→boot-load round-trip; key is `(provider, modelId)`, never name-colliding across providers.
- `UT-3` — source-scan: no provider/model identifier in the repair path beyond the classifier (the no-hardcode REG).
- `UT-4` — coalesce: adjacent tool-call/result pairs merge into compact messages; pairing invariants hold; newest user + system prompt untouched.
- `UT-5` — outbound-only: session record bytes identical before/after a cap repair.
- `IT-1` — fake model emitting a cap-400 → learned record written; second run loads it.
- `IT-2` — reactive path: cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once → success; second cap-400 → terminal.
- `IT-3` — pre-emptive: learned-cap model, count at `cap − margin` → compaction fires before the request; the request's array is under the cap.
- `E2E-1` — stub gateway replaying the incident transcript (>2048 messages): reactive repair heals the run; no permanent wedge.
- `E2E-2` — second run against the same stub with the learned cap: pre-emptive compaction, zero cap-400s observed.
- `REG-1` — no-hardcode source scan (AC5) in CI.
- `REG-2` — session-JSONL byte-identity across the repair (golden fixture).
- `REG-3` — no-cap models + existing token-compaction fixtures pass unmodified; a …

Now I have the ticket ACs. Let me get the issue comments too (2 comments). And then examine tests. Let me check key claims:

- AC2: persists across restarts + boot-loaded ✓ (CLI loads `~/.fah/model_caps.json`; persist on learn).
- AC4: pre-emptive ✓ in CLI + AutoCompactor.
- AC5: no hardcode — source scan test exists.
- AC6: pairing-safe ✓.
- AC7: JSONL byte-identical — coalesce is outbound-only; relief REPLACES the loop context with the compacted transcript... wait! The relief adopts the compacted transcript into the loop's `context`, which is the live transcript. Does that mutate the session JSONL? The compaction pass hides records in the session tree (structured compaction writes records to the session). Hmm — normal compaction also writes to the session (compaction records). "Byte-identical" claim in the PR: "transcript untouched until relief (AC7: JSONL byte-identical)". But the relief itself runs a compaction pass which writes compaction records to the session file — that's normal compaction behavior, same as over-window relief. AC7 says "session JSONL byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only)". Hmm, but the reactive repair includes a compaction pass per the ticket architecture ("coalesce + compaction pass → retry once"), and normal compaction DOES write to the session. The PR's claim "transcript untouched until relief" — coalesce doesn't touch the transcript; relief runs a real compaction which appends compaction records (same as any auto-compact). So AC7 is about the coalesce being outbound-only, presumably. Fine.

Now key checks remaining:
1. Issue comments (2) — may contain scope corrections.
2. The tests exist: message_cap_loop_test etc. Let me run them to check they pass (dart available?).
3. Potential correctness findings:

  a. **Cap heal + pairing heal ordering**: fine.
   
  b. **`_needsCapHeal` doesn't check that the request actually exceeded a cap count** — a transient 400 with matching text after a mid-turn... fine.
   
  c. **E1 ticket spec**: "cap-unknown → pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request (one pass), then retry". In the implementation, when cap is unknown, `coalesceTarget` is null and no pre-emptive trigger exists (learnedCapFor returns null since record has maxMessages == null). So for cap-unknown models, NO pre-emptive compaction ever fires — the implementation instead relies on relief-per-refusal. The ticket E1 says "the model is flagged cap-unknown → pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request (one pass)". The implementation doesn't fire pre-emptively for cap-unknown models (messageCapTriggerReached returns false for null cap). Is that a gap? Implementation choice: relief-only retry per refusal. The ticket says pre-emptive fires on the next request. Hmm — this is a deviation from the ticket edge case, but arguably deliberate (documented in code: "a cap-unknown refusal (E1) has no target — the retry rides the relief alone"). But then "pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request" is NOT implemented. Each refusal triggers a heal (one-shot per response, but every new response can heal once). Since each heal runs relief, the run doesn't wedge. The ticket's intent — "never a wedge" — is satisfied. The exact E1 mechanism differs. Could flag as SUGESTION/IMPORTANT deviation. Actually wait — there's a subtlety: `_needsCapHeal` requires `config.messageCapPolicy != null` and classified refusal; each new streamed response gets a fresh `_CapHealState`, so every refusal heals once. Good, no wedge.

  d. **Doc bug in message_cap.dart**: module doc says store is persisted at "`~/.fah/model-message-caps.json`" in PR description but code uses `model_caps.json`. PR description says `~/.fah/model-message-caps.json`; code comment in agent_cli says `model_caps.json`; message_cap.dart doc says "The CLI uses `<homeDir>/.fah/model_caps.json`". Minor doc inconsistency between PR text and code — not a code issue.

  e. **`ModelCapRecord.fromJson`**: `json['maxMessages'] is int` — JSON decode yields int for whole numbers, fine.

  f. **`keyOf` uses `\u{001F}` separator** — fine.

  g. **Security: none really** — local file store, no shell, no secrets.

  h. **`coalesceMessagesForCap` grouping across regionEnd** — as analyzed, an assistant message with tool calls just before the newest user message whose results come AFTER it would pull those results into a carrier before the user message, merging current-turn data into a "old turn" carrier. Violates "nothing after the newest user message is touched". Edge case; the loop's message structure: user message then assistant tool calls then results — results always immediately follow their assistant message in-order per turn. Interleaving with a user message between call and result happens with steering messages (the tool_pairing docs mention "result displaced from its call (stering interleave) → hoisted back"). So this IS a real scenario in this codebase! Steering can interleave user messages between a call and its result. If the newest user message is a steering message inserted between a tool call and its result, coalesce would merge the call AND its result (after the user msg) into a carrier placed before the user message — actually that keeps pairing and drops current-turn tool output content into a carrier summary. The tool result's content would be lost from the model's view (replaced by "[coalesced tool turn(s) ...]"). Hmm, the result was for a call made before the steering message; arguably "old turn". But the boundary condition `j < messages.length` (should arguably be `j < regionEnd` or stop at the first UserMessage) means a group could also span... let me think of a worse case: assistant call at i < regionEnd, then user message (newest) at regionEnd, then the result after. Group = [call, result], carrier placed before the user message. Newest user message stays verbatim. Pairing preserved. Content of the result hidden in carrier. Is that "dropping the running turn"? The running turn after the newest user message included that tool result — it gets merged away. The invariant doc says "nothing after it is touched". Deviation worth flaging. Severity: IMPORTANT (correctness of stated invariant, edge case).

  Actually wait, there's a subtler pairing bug: if the group spans the boundary, then in `merged`, the carrier (containing call+result) comes BEFORE the newest user message. Fine for providers. But if the result after the boundary does NOT belong to any call before the boundary — no issue.

  Also consider: assistant tool-call message whose results are missing within region but appear after boundary — same thing.

  Let me flag this as IMPORTANT.

  i. **`_carrierOf` label only names tool calls from AssistantMessages; a unit with a user message + result gets generic label** — fine.

  j. **Loop: after cap heal retry succeeds... the coalesceTarget remains armed for subsequent requests in the same response stream?** `_CapHealState` is per-response; after the retry within the same while loop iteration `continue`s to next iteration of the retry loop — `capState.coalesceTarget` still set, so the retried request is coalesced ✓. Once the response finishes (finished == null? no—retry returns a finished or null). If the retry yields `finished == null` (no terminal event) the loop breaks and returns; next `_streamAssistantResponse` call gets a fresh state. OK.

  But wait: what if the retried request succeeds with `finished == null` and the loop retries the turn later (`_streamAssistantResponse` called again)? Fresh capState, no coalesce — but the transcript was replaced by the relieved one. Fine.

  k. **Pre-emptive trigger double-check in `agent_cli_compaction.dart` `_runAutoCompact`**: `messageCap: _modelCaps.learnedCapFor(_agent.state.model)` — only learned value, config pin tier (`learnedCapOr` static helper) is not wired in the CLI. The ticket lists "Config override" as **second tier** — the store has `pin()` and `learnedCapOr` helpers but nothing calls them (dead code in this PR). Second tier was presumably out of scope. SUGESTION: `pin`/`remove`/`learnedCapOr` are currently unused (no caller) — dead API shipped. Check: grep for usages.

blocks.text:
rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Variants (`messages: array length 2051 exceeds limit 2048`, `array length N exceeds limit M`, `too many messages`, `messages count exceeds`) classify; non-overflow 400s (auth, bad request) do not. (`UT-1`)
- **AC2** — After one cap-400, `(provider, modelId)` is marked with the learned cap; the record persists across restarts and is boot-loaded. (`UT-2`, `IT-1`)
- **AC3** — Reactive: a classified cap-400 coalesces + runs one compaction pass + retries once; the retry succeeds; a second cap-400 surfaces the terminal; no infinite loop. (`IT-2`, `E2E-1`)
- **AC4** — Pre-emptive: a model with a learned cap triggers compaction when the live count reaches `cap − margin`, BEFORE the request; the request rides the compacted array (no doomed round-trip). (`IT-3`, `E2E-2`)
- **AC5** — No provider/model name is hardcoded anywhere in the repair path (source-scan asserts the classifier is the only built-in). (`UT-3`, `REG-1`)
- **AC6** — Coalesce preserves tool-call/result pairing (the `tool_pairing` repairer's invariants hold on the wire) and never drops the newest user message or the system prompt. (`UT-4`)
- **AC7** — The session JSONL is byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only). (`UT-5`, `REG-2`)
- **AC8** — A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today; token compaction semantics unchanged. (`REG-3`)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-1` — classifier: incident string + variants → overflow + parsed `M`; auth/other 400s unchanged; unparseable cap (`array length exceeds limit` without a number) → flagged cap-unknown.
- `UT-2` — learned-cap store: parse→record→persist→boot-load round-trip; key is `(provider, modelId)`, never name-colliding across providers.
- `UT-3` — source-scan: no provider/model identifier in the repair path beyond the classifier (the no-hardcode REG).
- `UT-4` — coalesce: adjacent tool-call/result pairs merge into compact messages; pairing invariants hold; newest user + system prompt untouched.
- `UT-5` — outbound-only: session record bytes identical before/after a cap repair.
- `IT-1` — fake model emitting a cap-400 → learned record written; second run loads it.
- `IT-2` — reactive path: cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once → success; second cap-400 → terminal.
- `IT-3` — pre-emptive: learned-cap model, count at `cap − margin` → compaction fires before the request; the request's array is under the cap.
- `E2E-1` — stub gateway replaying the incident transcript (>2048 messages): reactive repair heals the run; no permanent wedge.
- `E2E-2` — second run against the same stub with the learned cap: pre-emptive compaction, zero cap-400s observed.
- `REG-1` — no-hardcode source scan (AC5) in CI.
- `REG-2` — session-JSONL byte-identity across the repair (golden fixture).
- `REG-3` — no-cap models + existing token-compaction fixtures pass unmodified; a …

rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |

So coalesce destroys the result content that the normal repair path would have preserved. The model loses the tool output entirely in this edge case. The pairing is valid (no error), and there's a note, so it's not silent — but it loses data the existing repairer preserves.

Actually wait — in the coalesce path, the call was merged into a carrier (no longer a call on the wire), so the result has no call to hoist next to — repair has no choice but to drop it. This violates the spirit of "only whole tool-call/result pairs go" — the pair was NOT kept whole; the call went into the carrier and the result was dropped.

Hmm, but how likely is this scenario? The pairing docs say steering interleave displaces results from calls — "a result displaced from its call (stering interleave) → hoisted back next to it". So yes, real transcripts can have a user message between a call and its result. When cap coalesce fires on such a transcript, the result content is lost.

How severe? The cap heal fires only on a cap-400 refusal (rare, once per session typically). The retry then rides without that tool output. The model sees a note that the result was dropped. It can re-run the tool if needed. It's a graceful degradation with a notice — by design the coalesce drops content ("the full history stays in the session file"). The same happens for any whole pair: the pair's content is replaced by a carrier. Here the pair was SPLIT: call content dropped into carrier AND result dropped with a note. So actually the behavior is consistent-ish: all droppable-region content gets carrier'd. The inconsistency: the invariant doc claims whole pairs only. The split pair is a deviation from the documented invariant (AC6: "only whole tool-call/result pairs go"). Test says pairing invariants hold on the wire (they do), but the pair content is lost in two places.

rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Variants (`messages: array length 2051 exceeds limit 2048`, `array length N exceeds limit M`, `too many messages`, `messages count exceeds`) classify; non-overflow 400s (auth, bad request) do not. (`UT-1`)
- **AC2** — After one cap-400, `(provider, modelId)` is marked with the learned cap; the record persists across restarts and is boot-loaded. (`UT-2`, `IT-1`)
- **AC3** — Reactive: a classified cap-400 coalesces + runs one compaction pass + retries once; the retry succeeds; a second cap-400 surfaces the terminal; no infinite loop. (`IT-2`, `E2E-1`)
- **AC4** — Pre-emptive: a model with a learned cap triggers compaction when the live count reaches `cap − margin`, BEFORE the request; the request rides the compacted array (no doomed round-trip). (`IT-3`, `E2E-2`)
- **AC5** — No provider/model name is hardcoded anywhere in the repair path (source-scan asserts the classifier is the only built-in). (`UT-3`, `REG-1`)
- **AC6** — Coalesce preserves tool-call/result pairing (the `tool_pairing` repairer's invariants hold on the wire) and never drops the newest user message or the system prompt. (`UT-4`)
- **AC7** — The session JSONL is byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only). (`UT-5`, `REG-2`)
- **AC8** — A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today; token compaction semantics unchanged. (`REG-3`)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-1` — classifier: incident string + variants → overflow + parsed `M`; auth/other 400s unchanged; unparseable cap (`array length exceeds limit` without a number) → flagged cap-unknown.
- `UT-2` — learned-cap store: parse→record→persist→boot-load round-trip; key is `(provider, modelId)`, never name-colliding across providers.
- `UT-3` — source-scan: no provider/model identifier in the repair path beyond the classifier (the no-hardcode REG).
- `UT-4` — coalesce: adjacent tool-call/result pairs merge into compact messages; pairing invariants hold; newest user + system prompt untouched.
- `UT-5` — outbound-only: session record bytes identical before/after a cap repair.
- `IT-1` — fake model emitting a cap-400 → learned record written; second run loads it.
- `IT-2` — reactive path: cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once → success; second cap-400 → terminal.
- `IT-3` — pre-emptive: learned-cap model, count at `cap − margin` → compaction fires before the request; the request's array is under the cap.
- `E2E-1` — stub gateway replaying the incident transcript (>2048 messages): reactive repair heals the run; no permanent wedge.
- `E2E-2` — second run against the same stub with the learned cap: pre-emptive compaction, zero cap-400s observed.
- `REG-1` — no-hardcode source scan (AC5) in CI.
- `REG-2` — session-JSONL byte-identity across the repair (golden fixture).
- `REG-3` — no-cap models + existing token-compaction fixtures pass unmodified; a …

Interesting — the test at line 141 "pre-broken pairing" has a transcript: user(older), assistant(c1), result(x1), user(newest), result(orphan). Here the newest user message is at index 3, and an orphan result is after it. In coalesce, regionEnd=3. Units: [user older], [assistant c1 + result x1] (group stops at j=3 since messages[3] is a UserMessage, not ToolResult). Carrier merge with target 3: merged = [carrier1, carrier2, user(newest), result(orphan)] = 4 > 3, carriers.length=2 > 1 → merge carriers → 3 = target. Then repairToolPairing drops orphan. Output = [carrier, user(newest)]. OK.

Note in this test the grouping loop condition `j < messages.length`: for the assistant c1 group at i=1, j starts at 2: messages[2] is result x1 → added; j=3: messages[3] is UserMessage → break. Good.

Now the boundary-spaning case I hypothesized: assistant tool-call BEFORE the newest user message with its result AFTER it. Does the group loop pull the result across? `while (j < messages.length && answered.isNotEmpty)`: yes, if messages[j] across the boundary is a ToolResultMessage with matching id, it gets added to the group and coalesced. The comment in tool_pairing says steering interleaves can displace results from calls. So scenario: [user old, assistant(call c1), user(newest, steering), result(c1)]. newestUserIndex=2, regionEnd=2. Units: i=0: user → unit. i=1: assistant with call c1; j=2: user → break (not a result). So group=[assistant]. i=2 stops (regionEnd). So the result(c1) after the boundary stays in the tail. Pairing: carrier replaces assistant call... wait — the carrier merged the assistant call into a user-role carrier text, and the result(c1) remains in the tail answering a call that no longer exists on the wire as a call! Then `repairToolPairing(merged)` at the end: the result c1 is now orphaned (its call was merged into a carrier) → dropped or synthesized... Actually the carrier replaced the assistant message entirely, so the call c1 vanished from the wire while result(c1) remains → repairToolPairing drops the orphaned result. Hmm, that's actually pairing-safe but loses the result... but wait, that's only when the group DIDN'T capture the result.

But hold on — when CAN the group span the boundary? Group building breaks on any non-matching message. For the result to be after the boundary (after newest user msg), the call must before it with a user message in between. As shown, the group breaks at the user message. So the call merges into a carrier alone while its result sits in the kept tail → pairing repair drops the result. Content of the result lost. Is that "dropping the running turn"? The result answered a call from before the steering message. This is the "result displaced from its call (stering interleave)" case. repairToolPairing normally HOISTS the result back next to its call — but here coalesce destroyed the call first, so the hoist can't happen; the result is dropped as an orphan.

Wait — actually order matters: coalesce runs `repairToolPairing(merged)` at the end, so the final wire is pairing-valid. But compared to the no-coalesce path (where repair would hoist result next to call), the coalesce path LOSES the tool result content entirely. That's a real behavioral degradation in the steering-interleave edge case. Severity: this is an edge case (stering messages interleaved between call and result AND cap coalesce triggered). I'd rate IMPORTANT... but is the result truly lost? The carrier text says "tool turn(s) bash — N message(s) merged", and the result answering c1 is dropped by pairing repair. The model loses the tool output. In the non-coalesce path the pairing repair preserves it. Hmm.

Actually wait, let me re-check the group loop: `while (j < messages.length && answered.isNotEmpty)`. For the spanning case to occur, messages between call and result must all be ToolResultMessages matching... The loop breaks on the first non-matching message. A UserMessage between call and result breaks the loop. So spanning only happens when... nothing between, i.e., adjacent — then no boundary between them. So actually the group can NEVER span the newest-user boundary! Because any user message between the call and its result breaks the group; and the boundary IS a user message (unless newestUserIndex == -1, no user messages at all → regionEnd = last message, tail = 1 message). If newestUserIndex == -1, regionEnd = messages.length - 1, group loop `j < messages.length` could include the last message. Tail = [last]. Could a group at include the last message? If call at i and result at messages.length-1 adjacent — then regionEnd = length-1 = the result's index... but newestUserIndex == -1 means no user messages; if call at length-2 and result at length-1, group includes both; tail = messages.sublist(regionEnd) = [result]... wait regionEnd = length-1, so sublist(length-1) = [last message] = the result! And the group ALSO contains it — duplicated! Let me check: units built for in [0, regionEnd). Group at i=length-2: [call, result] with j reaching length. carriers include both. merged = [...cariers, ...messages.sublist(regionEnd)] = [..., call, result(carier merged as one carrier), result]. The result appears TWICE — once merged in the carrier, once verbatim in the tail! And the carrier is a UserMessage text, so pairing repair sees a lone result in the tail → orphan → dropped. OK so the duplicate gets dropped by repairToolPairing. Phew — no wire corruption. But this only occurs when there are NO user messages at all in the transcript (pure tool-call transcript). Edge of an edge; the repair catches it.

Hmm wait, actually also the FIRST case: newestUserIndex >= 0, call before boundary, result after boundary separated by the user message → group breaks at user message, call merges into carrier alone, result stays in tail → repair drops it as orphan. Actually wait — in the coalesce path, the call was merged into a carrier (no longer a call on the wire), so the result has no call to hoist next to — repair has no choice but to drop it. This violates the spirit of "only whole tool-call/result pairs go" — the pair was NOT kept whole; the call went into the carrier and the result was dropped.

Hmm, but how likely is this scenario? The pairing docs say steering interleave displaces results from calls — "a result displaced from its call (stering interleave) → hoisted back next to it". So yes, real transcripts can have a user message between a call and its result. When cap coalesce fires on such a transcript, the result content is lost.

How severe? The cap heal fires only on a cap-400 refusal (rare, once per session typically). The retry then rides without that tool output. The model sees a note that the result was dropped. It can re-run the tool if needed. It's a graceful degradation with a notice — by design the coalesce drops content ("the full history stays in the session file"). The same happens for any whole pair: the pair's content is replaced by a carrier. Here the pair was SPLIT: call content dropped into carrier AND result dropped with a note. So actually the behavior is consistent-ish: all droppable-region content gets carrier'd. The inconsistency: the invariant doc claims whole pairs only. The split pair is a deviation from the documented invariant (AC6: "only whole tool-call/result pairs go"). Test says pairing invariants hold on the wire (they do), but the pair content is lost in two places.

I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented invariant violated in a realistic transcript shape, silent-ish content loss of the current turn's tool output).

blocks.text:
rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Variants (`messages: array length 2051 exceeds limit 2048`, `array length N exceeds limit M`, `too many messages`, `messages count exceeds`) classify; non-overflow 400s (auth, bad request) do not. (`UT-1`)
- **AC2** — After one cap-400, `(provider, modelId)` is marked with the learned cap; the record persists across restarts and is boot-loaded. (`UT-2`, `IT-1`)
- **AC3** — Reactive: a classified cap-400 coalesces + runs one compaction pass + retries once; the retry succeeds; a second cap-400 surfaces the terminal; no infinite loop. (`IT-2`, `E2E-1`)
- **AC4** — Pre-emptive: a model with a learned cap triggers compaction when the live count reaches `cap − margin`, BEFORE the request; the request rides the compacted array (no doomed round-trip). (`IT-3`, `E2E-2`)
- **AC5** — No provider/model name is hardcoded anywhere in the repair path (source-scan asserts the classifier is the only built-in). (`UT-3`, `REG-1`)
- **AC6** — Coalesce preserves tool-call/result pairing (the `tool_pairing` repairer's invariants hold on the wire) and never drops the newest user message or the system prompt. (`UT-4`)
- **AC7** — The session JSONL is byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only). (`UT-5`, `REG-2`)
- **AC8** — A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today; token compaction semantics unchanged. (`REG-3`)

## Test plan

### Test matrix

- `UT-1` — classifier: incident string + variants → overflow + parsed `M`; auth/other 400s unchanged; unparseable cap (`array length exceeds limit` without a number) → flagged cap-unknown.
- `UT-2` — learned-cap store: parse→record→persist→boot-load round-trip; key is `(provider, modelId)`, never name-colliding across providers.
- `UT-3` — source-scan: no provider/model identifier in the repair path beyond the classifier (the no-hardcode REG).
- `UT-4` — coalesce: adjacent tool-call/result pairs merge into compact messages; pairing invariants hold; newest user + system prompt untouched.
- `UT-5` — outbound-only: session record bytes identical before/after a cap repair.
- `IT-1` — fake model emitting a cap-400 → learned record written; second run loads it.
- `IT-2` — reactive path: cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once → success; second cap-400 → terminal.
- `IT-3` — pre-emptive: learned-cap model, count at `cap − margin` → compaction fires before the request; the request's array is under the cap.
- `E2E-1` — stub gateway replaying the incident transcript (>2048 messages): reactive repair heals the run; no permanent wedge.
- `E2E-2` — second run against the same stub with the learned cap: pre-emptive compaction, zero cap-400s observed.
- `REG-1` — no-hardcode source scan (AC5) in CI.
- `REG-2` — session-JSONL byte-identity across the repair (golden fixture).
- `REG-3` — no-cap models + existing token-compaction fixtures pass unmodified; a …

rflow.dart` needs a pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M`.
- **C. A provider context refusal never triggers a self-healing repair.** The pairing-400 repair exists (`agent_loop.dart:1489`, issue #85) but a message-cap 400 does not; nothing coalesces/compacts the array under the cap and retries.

---

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Confirmed. In the steering-interleave case:
- The tool result content (`IMPORTANT TOL OUTPUT`) is dropped from the wire and only a note remains — whereas in the non-coalesce path `repairToolPairing` would HOIST the result back next to its call, preserving the output. So coalesce destroys the result content that the normal repair path would have preserved. The model loses the tool output entirely in this edge case. The pairing is valid (no error), and there's a note, so it's not silent — but it loses data the existing repairer preserves.

Actually wait — in the coalesce path, the call was merged into a carrier (no longer a call on the wire), so the result has no call to hoist next to — repair has no choice but to drop it. This violates the spirit of "only whole tool-call/result pairs go" — the pair was NOT kept whole; the call went into the carrier and the result was dropped.

Hmm, but how likely is this scenario? The pairing docs say steering interleave displaces results from calls — "a result displaced from its call (stering interleave) → hoisted back next to it". So yes, real transcripts can have a user message between a call and its result. When cap coalesce fires on such a transcript, the result content is lost.

How severe? The cap heal fires only on a cap-400 refusal (rare, once per session typically). The retry then rides without that tool output. The model sees a note that the result was dropped. It can re-run the tool if needed. It's a graceful degradation with a notice — by design the coalesce drops content ("the full history stays in the session file"). The same happens for any whole pair: the pair's content is replaced by a carrier. Here the pair was SPLIT: call content dropped into carrier AND result dropped with a note. So actually the behavior is consistent-ish: all droppable-region content gets carrier'd. The inconsistency: the invariant doc claims whole pairs only. The split pair is a deviation from the documented invariant (AC6: "only whole tool-call/result pairs go"). Test says pairing invariants hold on the wire (they do), but the pair content is lost in two places.

I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented invariant violated in a realistic transcript shape, silent-ish content loss of the current turn's tool output).

Wait — one more consideration: in the second probe, "no user messages at all" case — the result got duplicated into carrier AND tail then dropped with note. Output correct-ish. Fine.

1. **The E1 deviation**: ticket E1 says cap-unknown → "pre-emptive compaction fires on the next request (one pass), then retry". Implementation: no pre-emptive trigger for cap-unknown (learnedCapFor returns null → trigger never fires); instead each refusal gets relief+retry. Run never wedges either way. Deviation from the ticket edge-case spec, but arguably better. I'll note as SUGESTION/IMPORTANT? The AC list doesn't include E1 as AC; edges are guidance. The implementation heals per-refusal which satisfies "never a wedge". I'll flag as SUGESTION to align or document.

2. **Second-tier config override (pin/learnedCapOr)**: dead code — no callers anywhere. Ticket marks it "second tier" — maybe intentionally shipped for the follow-up. Dead public API in a fresh module; flag as SUGESTION.

## Goal — adaptive per-model message-cap handling: learn the cap from the error, coalesce + compact on refusal, trigger compaction before the cap (v2)

**A run can never wedge on a provider message-count cap: the cap is learned per model from the provider's own error, a cap refusal coalesces and compacts the context, and once learned, compaction fires before the cap is reached — with zero hardcoded provider/model tables.**

v1 of this card modeled `maxMessages` as a per-provider tuning knob. The user's correction: JoinGonka is a **gateway hosting many models**, each with its own limit — the cap is a property of the **model**, not the endpoint, and hardcoding provider/model tables is exactly what must not happen. The cap must be **discovered from the error text and learned per model**, then used as a **message-count compaction trigger**.

## Why this framing (supersedes v1)

- Retracted: `maxMessages` as a per-provider/baseUrl tuning entry — wrong granularity (one gateway, many models) and wrong source (hardcoded).
- Retracted: "pinned cap in the catalog" — the only built-in knowledge is the error-text classifier; the cap value itself is learned.
- Chosen: **learn by example, act pre-emptively**. The classifier recognizes the cap-400 shape (built-in, tiny, provider-agnostic); the specific limit `M` is parsed from the error and stored per model identity `(provider, modelId)`; a subsequent run compacts before the cap instead of after the failure.

## Architecture

```
request → cap-400 "array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048"
   │  overflow.dart classifier (NEW pattern; parses M=2048)
   ▼
learn: store (provider, modelId) → maxMessages=M        [persisted per-model store]
   ▼
repair (reactive): coalesce old tool-call/result pairs → send STRAIGHT to a compaction pass
   → retry once
   ▼
next runs (pre-emptive): before each request,
   messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin  ⇒  trigger compaction (message-count trigger)
   → request rides a compacted array, never a doomed round-trip
```

- **Cap discovery** — `overflow.dart` gains the classifier for `array length N exceeds limit M` / `messages: … exceeds limit …` (and returns the parsed `M`). Provider-agnostic: any model that emits this shape is handled; the regex is the ONLY built-in.
- **Learned-cap store** — a per-model record keyed `(provider, modelId) → maxMessages`, persisted next to the existing per-provider `model_cache.json` lifecycle (boot-load + background warm-refresh; same file family or a sibling). No provider/model tables in source.
- **Reactive repair (first occurrence)** — on a classified cap-400: **coalesce** the outbound array (merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs and old turns into compact messages — the user's "объединить сообщения"), then **send straight to a compaction pass** (the summary is the real message-count reducer), then retry once. A second cap-400 surfaces the terminal error.
- **Pre-emptive trigger (after learning)** — the auto-compactor gains a message-count trigger in addition to the token trigger: `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction BEFORE the request. Additive; the token trigger is untouched.

Invariants:
- Coalesce/compact never drops the newest user message or the system prompt; only whole tool-call/result pairs older than the cut point go.
- The session JSONL is byte-identical — repair is outbound-only (like `rewriteHistoryImages` and the pairing repair).
- The only hardcoded knowledge is the error-text classifier; no provider/model name appears in source.
- A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today.

## Capability surface

| Capability | Subject | Shape | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap-400 classifier | the provider error string | overflow.dart pattern for `array length N exceeds limit M` (+ variants), exposing parsed `M` | core |
| Learned per-model cap | the model identity `(provider, modelId)` | persisted record → `maxMessages`; boot-loaded; no hardcoded tables | core |
| Reactive repair | the outbound messages array | cap-400 → coalesce + compaction pass → retry once | core |
| Pre-emptive compaction trigger | the outbound messages array | `messageCount ≥ learnedCap − margin` fires compaction before the request | core |
| Coalesce step | the outbound messages array | merge adjacent tool-call/result pairs + old turns into compact messages (pairing-safe) | core |
| Cap notice | the user/UI | a trim/compaction fired by the cap names the cap and the count (no values) | core |
| Config override | a model's learned cap | user can pin/edit a model's cap in config (overrides the learned value) | second tier |
| Hardcoded cap tables | — | excluded: the user's explicit requirement — no provider/model maps in source | excluded |
| Per-endpoint caps | — | excluded: wrong granularity — one gateway hosts many models with different limits | excluded |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The exact incident string (`400 messages: array length 2049 exceeds limit 2048`) is classified as overflow AND yields parsed `M=2048`. Variants (`messages: array length 2051 exceeds limit 2048`, `array length N exceeds limit M`, `too many messages`, `messages count exceeds`) classify; non-overflow 400s (auth, bad request) do not. (`UT-1`)
- **AC2** — After one cap-400, `(provider, modelId)` is marked with the learned cap; the record persists across restarts and is boot-loaded. (`UT-2`, `IT-1`)
- **AC3** — Reactive: a classified cap-400 coalesces + runs one compaction pass + retries once; the retry succeeds; a second cap-400 surfaces the terminal; no infinite loop. (`IT-2`, `E2E-1`)
- **AC4** — Pre-emptive: a model with a learned cap triggers compaction when the live count reaches `cap − margin`, BEFORE the request; the request rides the compacted array (no doomed round-trip). (`IT-3`, `E2E-2`)
- **AC5** — No provider/model name is hardcoded anywhere in the repair path (source-scan asserts the classifier is the only built-in). (`UT-3`, `REG-1`)
- **AC6** — Coalesce preserves tool-call/result pairing (the `tool_pairing` repairer's invariants hold on the wire) and never drops the newest user message or the system prompt. (`UT-4`)
- **AC7** — The session JSONL is byte-identical before/after a cap repair (outbound-only). (`UT-5`, `REG-2`)
- **AC8** — A model with no learned cap behaves byte-identically to today; token compaction semantics unchanged. (`REG-3`)

Interesting — the test at line 141 "pre-broken pairing" has a transcript: user(older), assistant(c1), result(x1), user(newest), result(orphan). Here the newest user message is at index 3, and an orphan result is after it. In coalesce, regionEnd=3. Units: [user older], [assistant c1 + result x1] (group stops at j=3 since messages[3] is a UserMessage, not ToolResult). Carrier merge with target 3: merged = [carrier1, carrier2, user(newest), result(orphan)] = 4 > 3, carriers.length=2 > 1 → merge carriers → 3 = target. Then repairToolPairing drops orphan. Output = [carrier, user(newest)]. OK.

Note in this test the grouping loop condition `j < messages.length`: for the assistant c1 group at i=1, j starts at 2: messages[2] is result x1 → added; j=3: messages[3] is UserMessage → break. Good.

Now the boundary-spaning case I hypothesized: assistant tool-call BEFORE the newest user message with its result AFTER it. Does the group loop pull the result across? `while (j < messages.length && answered.isNotEmpty)`: yes, if messages[j] across the boundary is a ToolResultMessage with matching id, it gets added to the group and coalesced. The comment in tool_pairing says steering interleaves can displace results from calls. So scenario: [user old, assistant(call c1), user(newest, steering), result(c1)]. newestUserIndex=2, regionEnd=2. Units: i=0: user → unit. i=1: assistant with call c1; j=2: user → break (not a result). So group=[assistant]. i=2 stops (regionEnd). So the result(c1) after the boundary stays in the tail. Pairing: carrier replaces assistant call... wait — the carrier merged the assistant call into a user-role carrier text, and the result(c1) remains in the tail answering a call that no longer exists on the wire as a call! Then `repairToolPairing(merged)` at the end: the result c1 is now orphaned (its call was merged into a carrier) → dropped or synthesized... Actually the carrier replaced the assistant message entirely, so the call c1 vanished from the wire while result(c1) remains → repairToolPairing drops the orphaned result. Hmm, that's actually pairing-safe but loses the result... but wait, that's only when the group DIDN'T capture the result.

But hold on — when CAN the group span the boundary? Group building breaks on any non-matching message. For the result to be after the boundary (after newest user msg), the call must before it with a user message in between. As shown, the group breaks at the user message. So the call merges into a carrier alone while its result sits in the kept tail → pairing repair drops the result. Content of the result lost. Is that "dropping the running turn"? The result answered a call from before the steering message. This is the "result displaced from its call (stering interleave)" case. repairToolPairing normally HOISTS the result back next to its call — but here coalesce destroyed the call first, so the hoist can't happen; the result is dropped as an orphan.

Wait — actually order matters: coalesce runs `repairToolPairing(merged)` at the end, so the final wire is pairing-valid. But compared to the no-coalesce path (where repair would hoist result next to call), the coalesce path LOSES the tool result content entirely. That's a real behavioral degradation in the steering-interleave edge case. Severity: this is an edge case (stering messages interleaved between call and result AND cap coalesce triggered). I'd rate IMPORTANT... but is the result truly lost? The carrier text says "tool turn(s) bash — N message(s) merged", and the result answering c1 is dropped by pairing repair. The model loses the tool output. In the non-coalesce path the pairing repair preserves it. Hmm.

Actually wait, let me re-check the group loop: `while (j < messages.length && answered.isNotEmpty)`. For the spanning case to occur, messages between call and result must all be ToolResultMessages matching... The loop breaks on the first non-matching message. A UserMessage between call and result breaks the loop. So spanning only happens when... nothing between, i.e., adjacent — then no boundary between them. So actually the group can NEVER span the newest-user boundary! Because any user message between the call and its result breaks the group; and the boundary IS a user message (unless newestUserIndex == -1, no user messages at all → regionEnd = last message, tail = 1 message). If newestUserIndex == -1, regionEnd = messages.length - 1, group loop `j < messages.length` could include the last message. Tail = [last]. Could a group at include the last message? If call at i and result at messages.length-1 adjacent — then regionEnd = length-1 = the result's index... but newestUserIndex == -1 means no user messages; if call at length-2 and result at length-1, group includes both; tail = messages.sublist(regionEnd) = [result]... wait regionEnd = length-1, so sublist(length-1) = [last message] = the result! And the group ALSO contains it — duplicated! Let me check: units built for in [0, regionEnd). Group at i=length-2: [call, result] with j reaching length. carriers include both. merged = [...cariers, ...messages.sublist(regionEnd)] = [..., call, result(carier merged as one carrier), result]. The result appears TWICE — once merged in the carrier, once verbatim in the tail! And the carrier is a UserMessage text, so pairing repair sees a lone result in the tail → orphan → dropped. OK so the duplicate gets dropped by repairToolPairing. Phew — no wire corruption. But this only occurs when there are NO user messages at all in the transcript (pure tool-call transcript). Edge of an edge; the repair catches it.

Hmm wait, actually also the FIRST case: newestUserIndex >= 0, call before boundary, result after boundary separated by the user message → group breaks at user message, call merges into carrier alone, result stays in tail → repair drops it as orphan. So tool output lost vs. hoisted. Real but narrow. Let me write a quick sanity test to confirm behavior.

Also check: user messages between region... the group loop breaks at ANY message that's not a matching result — including AssistantMessages (parallel calls?) — pre-existing shape assumptions; pairing repair handles the rest.
